castle_keeper.text: The Normans raised this keep about nine hundred years ago, on a huge earth mound, to show Norwich exactly who was in charge now. It's one of the grandest Norman keeps in Europe.
It was a royal palace for barely five minutes, then a prison for six hundred years, until 1887. It's been a museum since 1894. The prisoners would be amazed. Mostly at the gift shop.
The outside's been refaced in pale Bath stone in the 1830s, copying the old pattern of blind arches. Underneath, the Normans are still there.

castle_teapots.text: We have one of the largest collections of British teapots in the world. Thousands. Some are shaped like cabbages, camels and cottages. One is shaped like a teapot, which feels like cheating.

castle_gaoler.text: In 1549 Robert Kett led thousands of Norfolk folk in a rebellion against the gentry fencing off the common land. They took Norwich, England's second city then. The King's army crushed them, and Kett was hanged from these very walls.
There's a plaque to him on the castle now, which says he was a leader of the struggle against oppression. Took them four hundred years, but they came round.
